boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase activities at Fresno State and Fresno neighborhood parks, with parking or registration caveats noted where applicable.

cards.title: Browse the Phebe Conley Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: See a rotating campus exhibition without paying admission.
cards.notes: Walk, bike or use transit to avoid the guest-parking charge, then meet inside during posted weekday gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery hang centered on Fresno State exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official page states that the Phebe Conley Art Gallery is free and open to the public and lists its regular hours.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free and the gallery is open to the public. Regular hours are Monday-Friday, 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; it is closed weekends, holidays and during announced seasonal closures. Guest parking costs $5, so arrive without a car to keep the hang at zero dollars.

cards.title: Take a Fresno State Campus Tour
cards.subtitle: Explore campus with a student ambassador on a free weekday tour.
cards.notes: Reserve an available weekday slot, gather your group at the designated meeting point and arrive 30 minutes early.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled, ambassador-led introduction to Fresno State’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Fresno State Outreach and Special Programs says its campus tours are free of charge and offers both virtual and in-person reservations.
cards.access_notes: The tour itself is free, but advance booking and weekday availability apply. Campus parking may require payment; use a no-cost arrival method to preserve the zero-dollar plan.

cards.title: Meet Up at Cary Park
cards.subtitle: Use a named Fresno neighborhood park for an outdoor group break.
cards.notes: Bring water and a blanket, choose an open shared area and keep the meetup informal so no facility reservation is needed.
cards.short_summary: An easy outdoor meetup in a city neighborhood park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno identifies Cary Park as a neighborhood park, and its official parks fee table states that neighborhood parks have no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: City neighborhood parks have no entrance fee. Use ordinary shared park space; reservations or organized facility use can carry separate requirements or charges.

cards.title: Catch Up at Rotary East Park
cards.subtitle: Gather outdoors at a no-fee Fresno neighborhood park.
cards.notes: Pick a daylight meetup time, bring your own water and use an unreserved common area for conversation or a casual walk.
cards.short_summary: A purchase-free setting for a daylight conversation outdoors.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno lists Rotary East Park within its park system, whose official fee table assigns no entrance fee to neighborhood parks.
cards.access_notes: No neighborhood-park entrance fee is required. Avoid reservable facilities or paid organized uses if the outing must remain free.

cards.title: Take a Break at Melody Park
cards.subtitle: Meet on the grounds of a named city neighborhood park.
cards.notes: Bring a reusable water bottle, find an available common area and leave scheduled program spaces open for participants.
cards.short_summary: A simple neighborhood-park reset that requires no purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno names Melody Park among its facilities, and the city’s parks fee table states that neighborhood parks charge no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: General neighborhood-park entry has no fee. Separate classes, reservations or limited programs may have their own registration rules.

cards.title: Walk and Talk at Todd Beamer Park
cards.subtitle: Turn a city neighborhood park visit into a free social walk.
cards.notes: Set a visible meeting point, walk together through open public areas and bring sun protection during warm weather.
cards.short_summary: A no-purchase walk-and-talk destination in north Fresno.
cards.evidence_claim: Todd Beamer Park is identified by the City of Fresno, whose official parks page states that neighborhood parks have no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: General entry to city neighborhood parks is free. Keep to open public areas and confirm any posted temporary restrictions upon arrival.

cards.title: Share a Picnic at Orchid Park
cards.subtitle: Bring food from home to a no-entrance-fee neighborhood park.
cards.notes: Use an open table or lawn without claiming exclusive space; bring everything from home and pack out the group’s waste.
cards.short_summary: A bring-your-own picnic option with no required transaction.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno identifies Orchid Park as a neighborhood park, and the city’s parks fee table says neighborhood parks have no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: Park entry is free, but exclusive use of the Orchid Picnic Pavilion requires a reservation. Use unreserved common space for a zero-dollar visit.

cards.title: Unplug at Tollhouse Park
cards.subtitle: Use a city neighborhood park for a screen-free group pause.
cards.notes: Put phones away for a short catch-up, stay in shared public areas and bring water rather than planning a purchase stop.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor pause designed around conversation, not spending.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno identifies Tollhouse Park within its neighborhood park system, for which the official fee table lists no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: Neighborhood-park admission is free. Posted closures, construction notices and rules still apply, so check conditions before gathering.

cards.title: Gather at El Dorado Park
cards.subtitle: Meet near campus in a city neighborhood park with no entrance fee.
cards.notes: Choose a well-used open area during park hours, bring water and keep the meetup small enough to avoid a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A close-to-campus public green-space meetup with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno lists El Dorado among its neighborhood centers and states in its official parks fee table that neighborhood parks have no entrance fee.
cards.access_notes: General neighborhood-park entry is free. Center programs, reserved facilities or organized activities may have separate access conditions.

cards.title: Plan a Group Reset at Einstein Park
cards.subtitle: Use a named Fresno neighborhood park for a free daytime meetup.
cards.notes: Agree on a short daylight window, meet in an open common area and bring any games, snacks or water from home.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, no-admission place for friends to decompress outdoors.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fresno identifies Einstein Park and its neighborhood center, while the official parks fee table specifies no entrance fee for neighborhood parks.
cards.access_notes: Entrance to city neighborhood parks is free. Use ordinary public space rather than reservable facilities, and follow all posted hours and rules.
